findings.reason: one sentence must change, and leaving it lets §16, which composes the fix from §12's list, be dispatched ahead of its upstream.
findings.text: the followup `f-wlsr-001` says "§3, §4 and §5 wait on §2; the other sections are independent", but `plan-section-depends-on` in the same document declares `s16` waits on `s12`; a coordinator reading the followup dispatches §16 before the inventory exists

findings.reason: a worker must either write a false row naming a comparison that no longer decides anything from that name, or fail a gate no truthful record can pass; the control must name a site still in the tree.
findings.text: §12's negative control requires the record to include "the admission gate-hold comparison against the configured local backend's name", yet §12's own preceding paragraph says that comparison "was corrected the same evening"; the gate-hold in `reckon/crew/admission/holds.py:104` now resolves a backend from `pointer["backend"]` and compares against no configured local backend name, so a correct search will not return the named site

findings.reason: the three need separate code paths and separate proof, and one verdict cannot close a node whose failures may sit in any of them; the third is not a harness-move property at all and belongs with the run-settlement work.
findings.text: §17's deliverable joins three mechanisms under one section: a refused lane change leaving the pointer unchanged, streams folded by the dialect that wrote each attempt, and a new scope-release command for a run that can be neither resumed nor promoted; its done-when carries four cases across them
